summary: Combat effects and environmental assets for a hostile, unfamiliar world.

sections.title: Fight through an alien landscape.
sections.body:
Conduit is a student-made 3D action-adventure game developed over a four-month semester. Players explore an alien tundra, investigate ruins, and fight mechanical and organic enemies.

I worked on the project’s art team, contributing combat effects and environmental props while also supporting the Simplified Chinese version and playtesting in Mainland China.

sections.title: Effects, assets, and implementation.
sections.body:
Character attack effects I created visual effects for character attacks, contributing to the moment-to-moment presentation of combat.

Hit effects I made effects associated with characters being hit. My work covered both the action and its immediate visual response.

Environmental props I modeled 3D objects for the game’s environments as part of the team’s shared asset production.

Conduit brought my effects work and 3D modeling into one playable team project. It also gave me a reason to think about the relationship between individual assets and the wider game experience.

sections.title: Making the game accessible to players.
sections.body:
Simplified Chinese localization

I translated game text from English into Simplified Chinese. The Steam page lists Simplified Chinese interface support in the released game.

Playtesting and outreach

I helped organize playtests and promotional activities for players in Mainland China, extending my contribution beyond asset production.

sections.title: Animated Anomalies.
sections.body:
Conduit was created as an RPI Games and Simulation Arts and Sciences capstone project. My role was part of the art team, alongside contributors working across design, programming, art, and audio.

Game overview, release information, and public media:  official Steam page .

sections.title: 穿行于异星景观
sections.body:
Conduit 是在四个月学期内完成的学生团队 3D 动作冒险游戏。玩家探索异星冻原、调查遗迹，并与机械和有机敌人战斗。

我参与美术团队，负责战斗特效与环境道具，同时支持简体中文版本和中国大陆玩家测试。

sections.title: 特效、资产与实现
sections.body:

这个项目将特效与建模工作放入同一个可玩的系统，也让我思考单个资产如何服务于整体体验。

title: Wands and Tomes
coverCaption: Team gameplay. My contributions are described below.
summary: One card. Two possibilities. Connecting card mechanics, playtesting, and 3D art.
role: Card mechanics · Selected 3D assets Simplified Chinese localization

sections.title: A spell, or a place on the board?
sections.body:
Wands and Tomes is a deckbuilding roguelike built around two uses for a card. A player can place its pattern on the board to form boxes and gain mana, or spend mana to cast its spell against an opponent.

The interesting design problem is the relationship between those two sides. A spell’s apparent cost can change dramatically when its pattern makes mana easy to recover.

sections.title: Design and art in the same system.
sections.body:
Card mechanics I contributed card functions and took part in discussions about mechanics, balance, and progression. Watching players use the cards became an important part of how I evaluated those decisions.

3D arena assets I produced selected 3D assets for the card battle arena as part of the art team.

Localization I worked on Simplified Chinese translation. This describes my contribution; it does not imply that every public build contains that localization.

sections.title: When Boomerang kept coming back.
sections.body:
The intended behavior

Boomerang was designed to be played repeatedly, as long as the player could pay its mana cost. That cost was meant to limit how much the player could do in a turn.

What players revealed

During playtests, I observed that its flexible board pattern made it unusually easy to recover the mana needed to play it again. The relationship between pattern and spell allowed repeated attacks far beyond what we had expected.

What changed in my approach

I began treating board placement and spell power as one design problem. A card’s damage and listed cost could not tell us enough on their own; we had to observe the sequences players could actually construct.

sections.title: A shared production.
sections.body:
The public project credits list me as an artist alongside Eugene Oh, Tyler Lin, Junhao Teng, and Nickolas Ho. The game is directed by Kevin Hacene, with programming, sound, music, and narrative contributions from the wider team.

Full team and third-party asset credits:  Wands and Tomes on itch.io .

sections.title: 施放法术，还是放入棋盘？
sections.body:
Wands and Tomes 是围绕卡牌双重用途展开的牌组构筑 roguelike。玩家可将卡牌图案放入棋盘，围成方框获取法力，或消耗法力对对手施放法术。

当图案使法力易于回收时，法术的实际成本也会发生变化。两者的关系是关键设计问题。

sections.title: 同一系统里的设计与美术
sections.body:
参与卡牌功能、机制、平衡和成长曲线讨论；通过观察玩家使用卡牌评估设计。作为美术团队成员制作部分卡牌竞技场 3D 资产，并参与简体中文翻译。

本地化描述的是个人贡献，不表示每个公开版本均已包含译文。

sections.title: 当 Boomerang 一次次回到手中
sections.body:
设计意图：只要玩家能支付法力，就能重复打出 Boomerang，成本本应限制每回合的行动。

测试发现：灵活的棋盘图案让玩家轻易回收法力，导致远超预期的连续攻击。

反思：棋盘放置与法术强度必须共同考虑，仅看伤害与标示成本不足以判断平衡，需要观察玩家实际构建的操作序列。

title: Afterlight / 余光
summary: An interaction with projected light leads into a small cinema, where the player can sit and watch a film.

sections.title: Light as an invitation
sections.body: The player begins from the projector viewpoint and aims light at an object. After the object has been illuminated long enough, control returns to a freely moving viewpoint. The player can then choose to sit and watch a film.

sections.title: Current prototype
sections.body: The Unity prototype includes object illumination, the transition to free movement, a seated viewpoint, and video playback. These describe the current working direction; final visuals and playtest evidence are still to be documented.

sections.title: Next documentation
sections.body: A short interaction recording, a final composition, a comparison of guidance and pacing, and a reflection will be added here. Production is currently paused.
